guide.title: How to File and Resolve a Grievance?
guide.subtitle: Follow the four essential stages of Katarungang Pambarangay for peaceful community resolution:
guide.step1_desc: Before issuing formal legal summonses, the Barangay extends a polite invitation for an amicable, private dialogue between both parties at the Punong Barangay's Office.
guide.step2_desc: If unresolved through informal dialogue, the grievance is officially docketed and formal Summonses (KP Form 9) are served for mediation presided by the Punong Barangay.
guide.step3_desc: If mediation does not yield a settlement within 15 days, a three-member Pangkat Tagapagkasundo is constituted from the Lupon to continue conciliation proceedings.
guide.step4_desc: Upon reaching agreement, an Amicable Settlement (KP Form 16) is executed having the force of a final court judgment. If unresolved after all statutory stages, a Certificate to File Action (CFA) is issued.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Barangay Justice
faq.q1: What disputes are covered under Katarungang Pambarangay?
faq.a1: Disputes between individuals residing in the same city or adjoining barangays involving offenses punishable by imprisonment not exceeding one year or a fine not exceeding ₱5,000, including neighborhood disagreements, boundary issues, small debts, and property damage.
faq.q2: What is the difference between a Paanyaya and a formal Summons?
faq.a2: A Paanyaya (Stage 0) is a polite, preliminary invitation for private dialogue before formal case docketing. A formal Summons (KP Form 9) carries legal statutory authority under RA 7160 commanding appearance before the Lupon.
faq.q3: Is there any fee or payment required to file with the Lupon?
faq.a3: No. All Katarungang Pambarangay mediation and dispute resolution services are completely free of charge for all residents of Barangay Tumana.
faq.q4: What happens if the respondent fails to attend the hearing?
faq.a4: If the respondent willfully fails to appear without justifiable cause after receiving summons, they forfeit the right to file counterclaims, and a Certificate to File Action may be issued or endorsed to the court.
faq.q5: What if the complainant does not show up?
faq.a5: If the complainant fails to appear without valid excuse, the complaint will be dismissed and no Certificate to File Action will be granted.
